--- title: "[ZPHResult]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-dataclass}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Proportional-hazards test results (Grambsch-Therneau). ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/greenwood/blob/feat-grays-test/greenwood/_cox.py#L63-L178){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.CLASS} ```python ZPHResult(transform, per_term, global_test, windows=None) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} A key assumption of the Cox proportional hazards model is that the hazard ratio between any two subjects is constant over time (hence "proportional"). When this assumption is violated (for example, if a treatment effect diminishes over time) the Cox model may produce biased estimates. The Grambsch-Therneau proportional hazards test checks this assumption by testing whether scaled residuals are correlated with time. `ZPHResult` holds the test results obtained from a fitted Cox model's `cox_zph()` method. It provides both per-term tests (one for each covariate) and a global test (jointly across all terms). Each test includes a chi-squared test statistic, degrees of freedom, and p-value. Results can be printed, accessed via dictionary keys, or exported to pandas/polars/ pyarrow DataFrames for further analysis or visualization. The test uses scaled Schoenfeld residuals, which have a known asymptotic distribution under the proportional hazards assumption. Large chi-squared values or small p-values (typically p < 0.05) suggest violation of the assumption. When the assumption is violated, stratified analysis or time-dependent covariate models may be more appropriate. ::: ## Attributes {.doc-attributes} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [transform]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The transformation applied to time when computing the test (e.g., identity, log, rank). [per_term]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [dict[str, dict[str, float]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Dictionary mapping each covariate name to `{chisq, df, p_value}` dict. [global_test]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [dict[str, float]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Dictionary with `{chisq, df, p_value}` for the joint test across all terms. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} A `ZPHResult` comes from a fitted model's `cox_zph` method. Fit a Cox model to the bundled `lung` dataset, run the proportional-hazards test, and print the result: ::: {#902ec070 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import greenwood as gw # Load data and fit a Cox model lung = gw.load_dataset("lung", backend="polars") y = gw.Surv.right(lung["time"], event=(lung["status"] == 2)) cox = gw.CoxPH().fit(y, lung[["age", "sex"]]) # Run the proportional-hazards test zph = cox.cox_zph() zph ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` ZPHResult(transform='identity', age: p=0.7065, sex: p=0.0992, GLOBAL p=0.2425) ``` ::: ::: ## Methods {.doc-methods}

### [to_frame()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Return the test table as a DataFrame. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/greenwood/blob/feat-grays-test/greenwood/_cox.py#L148-L178){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python to_frame(*, detail="global", format=None) ``` ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [detail]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["global"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Level of detail. `"global"` (default) returns the overall test (one row per term plus GLOBAL). `"windows"` returns per-window results when `breaks` was used in `cox_zph()`. Falls back to `"global"` when no windows are available. [format]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Output format: `None` (default), `"pandas"`, `"polars"`, or `"pyarrow"`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [pandas.DataFrame, polars.DataFrame, or pyarrow.Table]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A table with test statistics. With `detail="windows"`, includes `window` and `n_events` columns. ::: #### Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#caa82c50 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} import greenwood as gw lung = gw.load_dataset("lung", backend="polars") y = gw.Surv.right(lung["time"], event=(lung["status"] == 2)) cox = gw.CoxPH().fit(y, lung[["age", "sex"]]) zph = cox.cox_zph() zph.to_frame(format="polars") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}
